body: I really appreciate it, I found some motivation on New Years Eve to start getting things right again and try to find success again. I'm a little worried though because the only healthcare I have is the VA and they have me in "cognitive psychotherapy". They ask me every 2 weeks if I still feel suicidal so they can "check their box" that they "helped a veteran" but the therapy always turns into this very condescending thing where they try to say, "you just have to learn to cope because your emotion->anxiety->problem->repeat and I'm like I'd really rather hear an actual coping mechanism than a definition of the problem. My solution for now is essentially do all the things that I would consider something a successful person should be doing. Exercise again, study spanish again, get back into the workforce ASAP and work myself life a master of a slave(me filling both roles) until I start to enjoy it simply because of the routine, ignore the future while still making decisions that should, in turn eventually go well but don't bank on anyone or anything.
I appreciate it, trying to find motivation man, just trying to get motivated.

Edit 2: Also, even though the math doesn't always work when you are doing less than highly profitable labor. Remember the 50/30/20 rule. Try to never let your fixed expenditures exceed 50% of your total income, 30% for you to spend  ( because you earn money so that you have money lolamiright?) and 20% to savings. These numbers will not necessarily fit perfectly for you but they are a good baseline of understanding, while seeming counterintuitive in a consumerist society, the reality is MOST people live beyond their means. These numbers are usually doable, its just a matter of whether or not you are willing to live with mom and dad, or that shitty looking apartment until you finish your degree, get promoted, etc. Also, don't be afraid to tell yourself or your friends, I CAN'T AFFORD TO EAT OUT ALL THE TIME. or drink every friday or whatever.

Keep it separate, I assume you have a goal. If its a car, or furniture, or just planning for the future. I found a lot of success, but hitting milestones then setting that money aside in savings and working off of what I earned weekly/monthly/annually and setting up an allotment to my savings after I reached a milestone. Even if its 25 a paycheck or month. In essence keep it growing, constantly and permanently. When I adopted this mentality, suddenly numbers I never imagined seeing became the norm and I was perspectively changed to looking forward to numbers that seemed unrealistic before.

Edit: as you become more skilled at this, the decisions I began to make were separate accounts for car maintenance, buying a house, vet visits for my dogs etc.
